newsitem.title: UK: Van seized during Prince Charles N.Ireland visit.
newsitem.headline: Van seized during Prince Charles N.Ireland visit.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland seized a suspect van and sealed off an area of Belfast near a concert hall where Britain's Prince Charles was attending a gala on Tuesday.
"There is a suspect vehicle being checked. The area is sealed off. That's all I know at the moment," a police spokesman told Reuters.
Police said they did not know if a bomb was planted inside the vehichle but said they were taking no chances.

The van, which belongs to a flower company, was seized close to Belfast's showpiece 32 million pound ($52 million) Waterfront Hall by the banks of the River Lagan which the prince opened a few hours earlier.
The prince's bodyguards were alerted but the gala concert featuring opera singer Kiri Te Kanawa was not disrupted.
Security for the visit, the prince's first since Irish guerrillas stepped up a war on troops and police in the British-ruled province late last year, was increased.
He was accompanied by a large group of plain clothed bodyguards and uniformed police officers during the open air functions earlier in the day.

The outlawed Irish Republican Army, fighting to end British rule, abandoned a 17-month truce in February 1996 with a series of bombs in London. In October the IRA launched a wave of attacks in Northern Ireland and has killed two soldiers since then.
Charles has been a target for protests on previous trips to both sides of the divided island because he holds the largely ceremonial title of "colonel-in-chief" of the elite Parachute Regiment.
Paratroops shot dead 13 unarmed Irish nationalists during a Roman Catholic protest march in Londonderry city in 1972 in what became known as "Bloody Sunday".
Northern Ireland's Catholic minority say Britain should reopen an investigation into the killings and formally declare the victims innocent.
